claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this, I'll need to gather some information about your situation and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children who live with you?** If so, could you tell me their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child. My son Alex is 16 and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I have a few more questions to help me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Is Alex still in full-time education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in education at the moment. He left school recently and isn't studying anywhere right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I appreciate you letting me know. Before I can make a final decision, I need to check the specific eligibility rules to ensure I'm applying them correctly.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for waiting. Based on the information you've provided, I need to clarify one important detail:

**Since Alex is 16 and has recently left school without going into approved education or training, did he register with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services when he left?** 

This is important because if he did register, you may still be eligible for Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks after he left education.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with the careers service or anything like that. He just left school and has been at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have one more important question:

**Is Alex currently working? If so, is he working 24 hours or more per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all at the moment. He's just been at home since leaving school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. I now have all the details I need to assess your eligibility. Let me review the rules carefully and provide you with a decision.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Outcome: You are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

Child Benefit eligibility for children aged 16 and over depends on them being in approved education or training and under the age of 20. Since Alex is 16, no longer in education, and has not registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services, he no longer qualifies.

However, it's worth noting that if Alex does register with a careers service or the armed services in the future, you may be able to claim Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks from when he left school. I'd recommend contacting the Child Benefit Office if his circumstances change, such as if he starts approved education or training, or registers with a careers service.

reasonings: Alex is 16 years old. According to the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you can normally qualify for Child Benefit for a child aged 16 or over only if they are under 20 and stay in approved education or training. Alternatively, if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training, you can apply for Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks if they register with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. In Alex's case: (1) he is not in approved education or training, and (2) he has not registered with a careers service or the armed services since leaving school. Therefore, you do not qualify for Child Benefit for Alex.

Without meeting either of these conditions, Child Benefit eligibility for Alex has ended."}
